source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — Christian Religious Education, Grade 7
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). First published 2022, Revised 2024. Backfilled retroactively — skills already shipped in web/src/skills/creG7/ before this record was written. 6 strands: 1.0 Overview of Christian Religious Education, 2.0 Creation, 3.0 The Bible, 4.0 The Early Life of Jesus Christ, 5.0 The Church, 6.0 Christian Living Today (120 lessons total). Discrepancy noted: the front-matter Summary of Strands and Sub-Strands table names sub-strand 2.2 'Responsibility over Animals, Fish and Birds' — the body text (which carries the actual outcomes/experiences) titles the same sub-strand 'Stewardship over Creation'; body text is treated as authoritative, consistent with the precedent for other Grade 7 subjects' front-matter-vs-body discrepancies.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Importance of Studying Christian Religious Education
specificLearningOutcomes: analyse the importance of learning Christian Religious Education
discuss how Christian Religious Education promotes sound moral and religious values
compile five values needed to foster responsible living
apply the values acquired in their daily interactions
appreciate the learning of Christian Religious Education by living responsibly
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to study Christian Religious Education?
learningExperiences: brainstorm in small groups the meaning of Christian Religious Education
search the meaning of Christian Religious Education using a digital device or print materials and make short notes
discuss in teams the importance of studying Christian Religious Education and note key points
write a personal reflection journal on how learning CRE has changed his or her behaviour
list and share five values they need to live a morally upright life
use charts, posters, or flashcards to write messages that promote sound moral and religious values
compose a poem on how Christian Religious Education promotes sound moral and religious values
linkedLearningAreas: English: learners debate and discuss in groups.
Pre-Technical Studies: digital devices used to search for information.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Accounts of Creation
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate the biblical accounts of creation
discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation
identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts
value God's creation by conserving the environment
keyInquiryQuestions: How is the first account of creation different from the second account?
Why is it important to learn about the creation accounts?
learningExperiences: name features found in the natural environment
take a nature walk and appreciate God's creation in the school compound or the surrounding area
read Genesis 1:1-50 & 2:1-2:4A on the first creation account and Genesis 2:4B-25 on the second creation account
watch a video clip on the two biblical accounts of creation
summarise the main points on the first and second creation accounts
discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation and write short notes
in teams, use digital devices or print media to research on the attributes of God and write them on a chart
practice environmental conservation measures, such as planting trees or volunteering for clean-ups in the community
compose and sing a song on the second creation account
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: interaction with the environment during the nature walk.
English: reading Bible texts on the biblical accounts of creation.
Creative Arts and Sports: composing and singing a song on the second account of creation.
Pre-technical Studies: online search using digital devices on the attributes of God.

subStrands.name: 2.2 Stewardship over Creation
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over creation
discuss ways they can protect animals, fish, and birds
practise good stewardship by taking care of animals, fish, and birds
appreciate God's creation by conserving the environment
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you care for animals, fish, and birds?
How can you reduce conflicts between human beings and wild animals?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on how they care for animals, fish, and birds and make summary notes
read Genesis 2:15-20, James 3:7 and discuss the responsibilities given to human beings by God
discuss ways they can protect animals, fish, and birds
visit a zoo, animal park or farm and observe how animals, fish, and birds are taken care of, and write a report for presentation in class
write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on the importance of good stewardship over animals, fish, and birds
display the poster or chart in class or on the school notice boards
compose a poem on how they take care of animals, fish and birds in their environment
linkedLearningAreas: English: writing sensitisation messages on charts or posters.
Agriculture: brainstorming on how they take care of animals, fish, and birds.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Animal rights and welfare issues in education

subStrands.name: 2.3 Responsibility over Plants
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants
apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment
discuss how responsible use of plants contributes to economic growth
choose an income generating crop and plant it at home or school
desire to contribute to a healthy ecosystem
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you take care of plants?
How do you care for plants in your environment?
learningExperiences: list different types of plants found in the environment and how they take care of them
take a nature walk in the environment, observe different plants, draw them on charts, and display them in class
read Genesis 1:29, Genesis 2:15 and Psalm 104:14, summarise the teachings on charts and make a presentation
buzz on how they care for plants in their environment
brainstorm how responsible use of plants contributes to economic growth
interact with a resource person (environmentalist/forest officer/any other relevant person) and interview them on the economic benefits of plants
plant an income-generating crop either at home or school
take care of the plant until they get results
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: how they care for plants.
Agriculture: planting a crop at school or at home and caring for it.

subStrands.name: 2.4 Use of Natural Resources
specificLearningOutcomes: explain ways in which human beings use and misuse natural resources
explore the effects of misusing natural resources
discuss Biblical teachings on good use of natural resources
conserve the environment as responsible citizens
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you conserve the environment?
How do human beings benefit from natural resources?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on how their communities use natural resources
discuss how their communities have misused natural resources; write the points on charts and present them to the class
conduct an online or library research on how human beings have used and misused natural resources and make a PowerPoint presentation or use a chart
debate on the effects of destroying the environment
read Genesis 2:15, Exodus 23:10-11, and Deuteronomy 20:19 and discuss the biblical teachings on good use of natural resources/God's creation
write the points from the Biblical teachings on charts and present them to the class
jointly compose songs on the beauty of God's creation
engage in cleaning the school as a way of conserving the environment
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture: responsible use of God's creation/environment.
Pre-technical Studies: online search and presentation using PowerPoint slides.
English: composing a song and debating on the effects of destroying the environment.

subStrands.name: 3.1 Functions of the Bible
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the importance of the Bible in the society today
describe how the Bible promotes holistic growth
analyse how God's Word inspires different services among Christians today
appreciate the Bible as the inspired Word of God
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the Bible important in the life of a Christian?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on how the Bible is used in the society today and write the main points
read 2 Timothy 3:16-17, Hebrews 4:12 and outline lessons learnt
in teams, prepare PowerPoint slides or charts on the importance of the Bible and make a presentation in class
write summary points on how the Bible is used in spreading the Word of God
discuss how the Bible promotes the spiritual, moral, social, emotional, and intellectual growth of a person
list different services offered by Christians in the local communities
make a presentation on how God's word inspires different services among Christians today
participate in different services in their local community and write a journal
compose a song about the Bible
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading and discussing the Bible texts provided.
Pre-technical Studies: digital devices used to prepare PowerPoint slides.
Creative Arts and Sports: composing and singing a song about the Bible.

subStrands.name: 3.2 Divisions of the Bible
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the two divisions of the Bible
categorize the books in the Old and New Testament
appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to know the books of the Bible?
learningExperiences: brainstorm in pairs the two major divisions of the Bible
use flashcards to sort and arrange books of the Bible sequentially
use a digital device or the Bible to read out books in the Old and New Testament
jointly outline the four major categories of books in the Old Testament
team up to outline the four major categories of books in the New Testament
share tasks to design a bookmark on the books of the Bible and place it in their Bible story Book or the Bible
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics: sorting and arranging sequentially books of the Old and New Testament.

subStrands.name: 3.3 Bible Translation
specificLearningOutcomes: identify versions of the Bible used today
discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages
describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages
examine the social and economic effects of translating the Bible into local languages
appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to translate the Bible into different languages?
learningExperiences: mention versions of the Bible used in Kenya today
buzz on the reasons that led to the translation of the Bible into local languages
discuss Bible translation from the original languages (Hebrew, Greek) to local languages
brainstorm on the benefits of Bible translation
interview a resource person on the social and economic effects of translating the Bible to local languages
debate on the topic, 'Bible translation is still necessary today'
linkedLearningAreas: English: interviewing resource persons on the social and economic effects of translating the Bible into local languages.

subStrands.name: 3.4 Leadership in Israel: Moses
specificLearningOutcomes: describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel
identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus
outline leadership qualities they can emulate from Moses
apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives
choose leaders of integrity to foster stable governments
value responsibility by choosing credible leaders
keyInquiryQuestions: Why was leadership in Israel important?
learningExperiences: discuss in groups characteristics of a good leader
brainstorm on qualities they consider when choosing leaders at school or church
read Exodus 2:11-13, 3:1-2, 11-12, and 6:12, and list ways God prepared Moses for leadership
read Exodus 14:13-16, 21, 15:22-25, 18:5-10, 18:17-24; Deuteronomy 4:1-3, 5, 6, and discuss roles performed by Moses during the Exodus
conduct an online or library research on leadership qualities portrayed by Moses and summarise them on a chart
write a journal on how to be a good leader at school, church, and in the community
debate on the advantages of choosing leaders of integrity in today's society
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: researching and making notes on leadership qualities portrayed by Moses.

strands.name: 4.0 The Early Life of Jesus Christ

subStrands.name: 4.1 Prophecies about the Messiah
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah
elaborate the fulfilment of the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah
value the fulfillment of the Old Testament prophecies
keyInquiryQuestions: How were the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah fulfilled?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the word prophecy and share findings with the class
buzz on the meaning of the word 'Messiah'
write the meaning of the word Messiah on flashcards
read Isaiah 7:13-14, 9:6-7, and Jeremiah 23:5-6, and list the prophecies about the coming of the Messiah
write the Bible texts on the coming of the Messiah on flashcards and place them in their note books for reference/revision
watch a video clip on prophecies about the Messiah
conduct an online or library research on fulfilment of prophecies about the Messiah and present the points in class
team up to read Matthew 1:18-23 and Luke 1:26-38 and summarise the fulfillment of the Old Testament prophecies
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading Bible texts and brainstorming on the meaning of the term 'Prophecy'.
Social Studies: discussing the message about peace in relation to the coming of the Messiah, the prince of Peace.

subStrands.name: 4.2 John the Baptist — A Precursor to the Messiah
specificLearningOutcomes: elaborate the annunciation and birth of John the Baptist
relate the birth of John the Baptist to the coming of the Messiah
interpret John's description of the Messiah in Luke 3:16 and John 1:29-30
discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18
apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life
desire to live a morally upright life
keyInquiryQuestions: How is John the Baptist a precursor to the Messiah?
learningExperiences: read Luke 1:5-25 on the annunciation of the birth of John the Baptist and retell the story
read Luke 1:57-66 and make short notes on the birth of John the Baptist
role-play the annunciation of John the Baptist and record it using a digital device
read Luke 3:16 and John 1:29-30 and write the main points on flash cards
compose a poem on how the birth of John the Baptist prepared the way for the coming of the Messiah
read Luke 3:7-18 and discuss the message of John the Baptist
list the values outlined in the message of John the Baptist
dramatize ways of applying values acquired from the message of John the Baptist in daily life
sing a song related to the mission of John the Baptist
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading Bible texts and brainstorming on the meaning of the term 'Prophecy'.
Social Studies: discussing the message about social justice and responsibility.

subStrands.name: 4.3 The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ
specificLearningOutcomes: elaborate the annunciation and birth of Jesus Christ
describe the dedication of baby Jesus
relate the dedication of Jesus to similar practises in the church today
narrate the story of Jesus Christ in the Temple
identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ
acknowledge the gift of our Saviour by celebrating His birth
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ?
learningExperiences: read Luke 1:26-38 and Luke 2:1-20 in turns
brainstorm on the events that took place during the annunciation of the birth of Jesus Christ
collaboratively make a presentation on the annunciation of the Birth of Jesus Christ using PowerPoint slides or charts
watch a video clip on the birth of Jesus Christ and write the key points on a chart
share experiences of how children are dedicated in church today
mention the importance of dedicating babies in church today
read Luke 2:22-38 in turns and make short notes
in groups discuss the importance of the dedication of baby Jesus
read Luke 2:41-52 and retell the story of Jesus Christ in the Temple
create a mind map on the story of Jesus Christ with the elders in the Temple
in pairs write on flashcards values that Christians learn from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: Jesus's parents were concerned about His welfare.
English: making presentations in class on the annunciation and the birth of Jesus Christ.

subStrands.name: 5.1 Selected Forms of Worship
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the teachings on praise and thanks giving from the scriptures provided
discuss the importance of prayer and fasting
explain teachings on prayer and fasting from the scriptures provided
practise the teachings of Jesus Christ on prayer and fasting
take part in different forms of worship at home, church and in school
pray to God always to grow spiritually
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is prayer and fasting important in the life of a Christian?
learningExperiences: define the word 'Worship'
share experiences of how worship is done in his or her church
jointly read Exodus 15:20-21, Psalm 30:11-12, 96:1-2, 150:1-5, Ephesians 5:19; and outline the teachings on praise and thanksgiving
brainstorm in groups why prayer and fasting is an important form of worship
use a digital device or a poster to summarise points on the importance of prayer and fasting
team up to read Luke 4:1-2, Acts 13:1-3, Matthew 6:9-13, 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18
outline lessons learnt from the Bible texts and make a presentation using a digital device or a chart
read Matthew 6:16 and discuss how one should conduct himself or herself when fasting
journal how they practise different forms of worship
participate in worship at home, church and in school and write a report for presentation in class
brainstorm on the topic 'we were created to worship God'
in collaboration, read and compose a song based on Psalms 150:1-5
sing a song on the Lord's prayer
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts and Sports: singing a song on the Lord's Prayer.
Pre-technical Studies: making a presentation using a digital device.

subStrands.name: 5.2 Role of the Church in Education and Health
specificLearningOutcomes: appraise the contribution of the Church towards education and health
identify barriers to effective Church mission work in Kenya today
recommend solutions to barriers hindering effective mission work
appreciate the contribution of the Church in education and health
keyInquiryQuestions: How does the church support education and health?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on healthcare facilities established by churches in their communities
use google maps/County maps to identify healthcare facilities established by the church in Kenya today
carry out an online research on the role of the church in education and health and present the findings in class
discuss and summarise on charts, barriers to effective church mission work
discuss solutions to barriers hindering effective mission work in Kenya today
interview vetted resource persons on the contribution of the Church to education and health in Kenya today
linkedLearningAreas: English: interviewing vetted resource persons on the contribution of the Church in education and health.
Social Studies: using google maps to identify schools and healthcare facilities established by the church.

subStrands.name: 6.1 Human Sexuality
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the meaning of human sexuality for holistic development
discuss healthy and unhealthy relationships for responsible living
discuss the circumstances that lead to unhealthy relationships
outline the consequences of engaging in sex before marriage
compile values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour
utilize values and life skills acquired to form healthy relationships
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you maintain sexual purity as a youth?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the meaning of human sexuality
discuss the meaning of healthy and unhealthy relationships
outline the teachings in 1 Corinthians 6:9 and 18 and summarise lessons learnt
read Philippians 4:8-9 and Galatians 5:23, reflect on it and write a journal on values and life skills they apply as they relate with others
write 1 Thessalonians 4:3 on a flash card and recite it
discuss circumstances that can lead to sexual temptations
brainstorm on how to avoid temptations/tempting places
role-play on how to overcome a tempting situation
list/mention the negative effects of engaging in sex before marriage
listen to and engage a resource person on values and life skills guiding good morals and summarise key points
reflect on their relationships and journal their resolve to remain chaste until marriage as they depend on God's strength/prayer
carry out a debate in class on 'it is possible for a young person to remain chaste until marriage'
compose and recite a poem titled 'Lord help me overcome temptations'
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading scriptures, debating and expressing themselves confidently.
Creative Arts and Sports: composing and reciting a poem.
Integrated Science: listing the negative effects of engaging in sex before marriage.

subStrands.name: 6.2 Christian Marriage and Family
specificLearningOutcomes: discuss the biblical teachings on marriage and family
explain ways the church promotes values among young people before marriage
identify values needed to maintain stability in families
appreciate the family as a sacred institution ordained by God
keyInquiryQuestions: How does a good marriage contribute to stability in the society?
learningExperiences: read Genesis 2:23-24 and Ephesians 5:22-33 in turns and summarise the main biblical teachings about marriage
read Exodus 20:12, Psalm 127:3-5, Ephesians 6:4 and note the key points
list values needed by young people before they enter into marriage
interact with a religious leader or a resource person and interview them on how the church promotes values among young people before marriage
carry out an online or library research on values needed to contribute towards stable families
write key messages on charts or flashcards on values needed to contribute towards stable families
role-play a stable Christian family
compose and recite poems on 'God is the centre of stable families'
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: appreciating marriage and families as important institutions necessary for stability in society.
English: composing and reciting poems.

subStrands.name: 6.3 Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Use
specificLearningOutcomes: identify drugs commonly abused by youths in Kenya today
discuss reasons why young people abuse drugs today
explore the effects of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse on an individual and the family
read the scriptures provided on the effects of alcohol, drug and substance abuse
recommend values and life skills needed to stay free from alcohol, drug and substance abuse
utilise values and life-skills acquired to live an alcohol, drug and substance-free life
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do young people abuse drugs and alcohol today?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the meaning of alcohol, drug and substance abuse and share findings with the class
list drugs commonly abused by youths in Kenya today
discuss the causes of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse today
research on persons who abused drugs and the effects it had on them
conduct an internet or library research on the effects of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse and make a presentation in class
read 1 Corinthians 3:17, 1 Corinthians 6:10, Ephesians 5:18, Proverbs 20:1, Proverbs 23:29-35, Proverbs 31:6 and Isaiah 5:11
share lessons learnt from the scriptures and make notes
debate on life skills and values needed to avoid alcohol, drug and substance abuse
listen to a resource person sharing success stories on overcoming alcohol, drug and substance abuse as a youth
reflect and write a journal on ways to avoid alcohol, drugs and substance abuse as a Christian youth
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: negative effects of alcohol, drug and substance abuse.
Pre-technical Studies: online or library research on causes and effects.
Social Studies: causes of alcohol, drug and substance abuse and values needed for responsible living.

subStrands.name: 6.4 Gambling
specificLearningOutcomes: identify types of gambling in Kenya today
discuss five causes of gambling
outline teachings on money and wealth from the scriptures provided
examine the effects of gambling on individuals and families
outline teachings on true riches from the scriptures provided
utilize acquired skills and moral values to live a gambling free life
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do young people engage in gambling today?
learningExperiences: share collaboratively what they know about gambling
brainstorm on the meaning and types of gambling
jointly use digital devices or read relevant textbooks on the causes of gambling today
share with classmates how to avoid negative peer influence that can lead to gambling
listen to and engage a resource person on how to avoid gambling
read 1 Timothy 6:10, Proverbs 13:11 and Proverbs 28:20-22, Ephesians 4:28 and summarise the key points on charts for presentation in class
role-play the effects of gambling on individuals and families
read Matthew 6:19-21, Hebrew 13:5, 1 Timothy 6:17-19 and outline lessons learnt on true riches
conduct an online or library research on values and life skills needed to avoid gambling
debate on 'skills and values needed to avoid gambling'
recite 1 Corinthians 6:12 and explain the meaning as a memory verse
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: effects of gambling on an individual and families.
Creative Arts and Sports: role-playing the effects of gambling on individuals and families.

subStrands.name: 6.5 Social Media
specificLearningOutcomes: identify different social media platforms used by young people today
describe ways of using social media responsibly
examine ways in which social media is misused today
discuss ways they should respond to cyberbullying
recommend values and life skills needed for responsible use of social media
apply Christian values as they use different social media platforms
desire to use social media responsibly
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you be cautious when using social media?
learningExperiences: list different social media platforms they interact with
brainstorm on the dangers of chatting or meeting with online strangers
list precautions they need to exercise whenever they use social media
discuss how social media is misused today and make PowerPoint slides for presentation in class
brainstorm on cyberbullying and how to respond
write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on values and life-skills needed when using social media platforms
interview a resource person on responsible use of social media
write personal reflections on how to use social media responsibly
linkedLearningAreas: English: interviewing a resource person on responsible use of social media.
Pre-technical Studies: discussing how social media is misused today and making a PowerPoint presentation.
